1  THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 30(1) OF THE EMPLOYEES COMPENSATION ACT, PRAYING TO SET ASIDE THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 26.11.2015 PASSED BY THE LEARNED SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE & JMFC LINGSUGUR, IN ECA NO.144/2014, BY AWARDING APPROPRIATE AND ADEQUATE COMPENSATION AS PRAYED IN THE CLAIM PETITION, IN THE INTEREST OF JUSTICE AND EQUITY.

THIS MFA HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED FOR JUDGMENT ON 02.02.2023, COMING ON FOR PRONOUNCEMENT OF JUDGMENT THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:-
 JUDGMENT Being aggrieved by the dismissal of the petition filed by her under Section 10 of the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for short) seeking compensation for the death of her husband Gaddeppa in a motor vehicle accident dated 30.12.2011, passed in ECA No.144/2014 by the Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Lingasugur, petitioner is before this Court under Section 30(1) of the Employees Compensation Act, 1923, with a prayer to set aside the impugned judgment and award and grant compensation.
2. For the sake of convenience the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
3. FACTS: It is the case of the petitioner that her husband i.e., deceased Gaddeppa was working as a Labour under respondent No.1 in his Tractor bearing registration No.KA-36/TB-3168 and Trailer bearing Chassis No.62/2011 (hereinafter referred to as 'the offending vehicle' for short).
It was insured with respondent No.2.
On 30.12.2011, as per the instructions of respondent No.1, deceased was proceeding in offending vehicle with other labourers from Mudgal to their native village with load of Bricks for unloading.
At about 4.00 p.m., near Kudalasangappa Daggi, on Mudgal - Nagaral road, the driver of the offending vehicle drove the same in a high speed, in a rash or negligent manner.
As a result, the Tractor and Trailer turned turtle.
In the said accident, Gaddeppa sustained grievous injuries.
Initially, he was taken to Government Hospital, Lingasugur and from there shifted to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru.
However, he died while undergoing treatment and the driver and other labourers also sustained injuries.

The death of Gaddeppa was arising out of and during the course of his employment under respondent No.1 and therefore, respondent No.2 is liable to indemnify respondent No.1 and prays to allow the petition by granting compensation in a sum of Rs.8,00,000/-.

4. After service of notice, respondent No.1 - owner of the offending vehicle appeared and filed written statement denying that deceased Gaddeppa was engaged by him as a labourer in the offending vehicle.
He also denied that on the date of accident, deceased Gaddeppa and other labourers were proceeding in Tractor and Trailer loaded with Bricks for unloading the bricks.

He has specifically denied that the death of Gaddeppa occurred in the accident arising out of and in the Smt. Mallavva @ Mallamma W/O Gaddeppa vs Sri Mahantesh S/O Hanumappa Rathod, And ... on 22 May, 2023

2 course of the employment under him.

Alternatively, in the event of allowing the petition, respondent No.2 may be directed to pay the compensation as at the time of the alleged accident, the offending vehicle was insured with it and prays to dismiss the petition against him.
5. Though duly served with notice, respondent No.2 has remained absent before the Tribunal.
6. Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.
7. Petitioner got examined himself as PW-1 and relied upon Exs.P-1 to P-10.
8. Respondent No.1 is examined as RW-1 and Exs.R-1 and R-2 are marked.

9. After considering the oral and documentary evidence placed on record and hearing the arguments of both parties, the Tribunal has dismissed the petition holding that deceased was not working as labourer under respondent No.1 and for the purpose of claiming compensation, such false pleadings were put forth.
10. Aggrieved by the same, petitioner has filed this appeal contending that the impugned judgment and award are contrary to the material placed on record.

The Tribunal has misinterpreted Section 2(dd) of the Employees Compensation Act and failed to take into consideration extended definition of employee with respect to Schedule-II clause (XXVI) of the Act and came to a wrong conclusion that the relationship between deceased and respondent No.1 is not proved.
The Tribunal has misread the contents of Ex.P-2 i.e., complaint.
It has failed to appreciate the admission given by respondent No.1 during his cross- examination regarding the relationship of employer and employee between him and the deceased.
11. During the course of arguments, learned counsel for the appeallant reiterated the grounds urged in the appeal and prays to allow the appeal or atleast remand the matter for reconsideration.
12. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.1 supported the contention of the petitioner and prays to remand the matter.
13. However, learned counsel for respondent No.2 supported the impugned judgment and award and prays to dismiss the appeal.

14. Heard arguments and perused the record.
15.

The appeal is admitted on the following substantial question of law:
i) Whether the court below is right in dismissing the claim of the petitioner/appellant without considering the admission given by respondent No.1?
16.

Thus, petitioner maintained a petition under Section 10 of the Workmen's Compensation Act,
1923 contending that on the ill-fated day i.e., on 30.12.2011 her husband along with other labourers Smt. Mallavva @ Mallamma W/O Gaddeppa vs Sri Mahantesh S/O Hanumappa Rathod, And ... on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125148285/
3 were traveling in the offending vehicle as labourers in order to unload Bricks and accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
It is the definite case of the petitioner that her husband/deceased Gaddeppa was an employee under respondent No.1 and respondent No.1 had engaged him to unload the bricks.
Therefore, the death of Gaddeppa has occurred arising out of and during the course of his employment and as such, respondent No.1 is liable to pay compensation.

Since the vehicle was insured with respondent No.2, it is liable to indemnify respondent No.1.
17.
However, respondent No.1 in the written statement has specifically disputed the relationship of employer and employee between him and the deceased Gaddeppa.
He has specifically denied that the deceased was engaged as labourer to work in the offending vehicle and more particularly, on the date of the accident.
In the light of specific denial of relationship between him and the deceased as employer and employee, heavy burden is on the petitioner to prove the same.
18. In respect of the accident in question, the son of the deceased by name, Shankrappa has filed the complaint on the same day at 11.30 p.m.

In the said complaint, he has stated that on the date of incident i.e., on 30.12.2011 at 10.00 a.m., his father along with uncle Jadeppa and one Hanumanthappa engaged the offending vehicle in order to transport Sajje (Pearl Millet) grown in their land.
Along the said load of sajje, deceased and other two traveled to Mudgal APMC.

In the evening, when they were returning to the village in the same vehicle i.e., the offending vehicle, the driver of the offending vehicle loaded bricks belonging to some other person and when they were returning to the village, accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving.

19. Nowhere in the complaint, it is stated that deceased and others were loaders in the said Tractor and Trailer and they were proceeding to the destination where the bricks were required to be unloaded by them.

As per the earliest version coming on record, it is evident that though deceased and others transported Sajje in the offending vehicle in the morning and sold the same at the APMC,
Mudgal, in the evening they were just traveling in the offending vehicle as gratuitous passengers.

Only in order to claim compensation for the death of the deceased, petitioner has created a story of deceased being the employee under respondent No.1.
20.
Rightly, respondent No.1 in his written statement has disputed the relationship of employer and employee between him and the deceased.
However, it appears at the time of giving evidence, he was persuaded to admit that deceased was an employee under him in order to see that compensation is paid through respondent No.2.

Consequently, during the course of examination in chief as well as during the cross examination by the petitioner, respondent No.1 who is examined as RW-1 has admitted that deceased was an employee under him.
As rightly, observed by the Tribunal, his evidence and admission are contrary to the defence taken by him and as such, cannot be accepted.

Apart from the admission of RW-1 absolutely no other oral or documentary evidence is placed on record to corroborate the contention of the petitioner that deceased was an employee under respondent No.1.
21.
Considering all these aspects, the Tribunal has rightly rejected the contention of the petitioner and dismissed the petition.

On the date of accident, though in the morning, deceased and others transported sajje owned by them in the offending vehicle, in the evening they were traveling in the offending vehicle to reach their native village as gratuitous passengers.

Only to claim compensation,
petitioner has come up with a story that deceased was an employee under respondent No.1, which she has failed to establish.

22. Thus, from the above discussion, this Court is of the considered opinion that there are no justifiable grounds to interfere with the impugned judgment and award and accordingly, the substantial question of law is answered in the affirmative and I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (
i) Appeal filed by the appellant is dismissed.
